title: Validate native CUDA scientific outcomes on an independent collection
body:
PR #65 provides useful prospective evidence on one RELION tutorial collection; its 22 held-out movies share the same collection/detector/specimen. Broader support needs a second collection, not a retuned threshold on those same movies.

## Plan for an independent Opus task
1. Inspect #61/#65, the final #66 candidate and available legal/shareable datasets; propose a bounded data subset and storage/compute estimate before downloading a large collection.
2. Freeze source, input hashes, correction options and scientifically meaningful primary margin before inspecting held-out outcomes.
3. Use matched particles/halfsets/downstream settings and an independent refinement check, with sensitivity controls; record what each can detect.
4. Compare native CUDA against the same-source CPU, preserving relative-RMSE diagnostics and all failed/inconclusive outcomes.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] Independent specimen/collection provenance and reproducible acquisition recipe.
- [ ] Prospective protocol and margins with movie/collection-level uncertainty, not pixel pseudoreplication.
- [ ] Deliberate harmful control detected by primary endpoint; weak CTF-only signals cannot substitute.
- [ ] Pass/fail/inconclusive outcomes and exact artifact provenance published; no gate fitted to make CUDA pass.
- [ ] Claims limited to evaluated modes; scientific study never substitutes for failure handling or reproducibility.

## Scope / dependencies
Research only until #66 has a pinned candidate; no production kernel changes. This is ready for planning and suitable for a later Opus assignment. Use cpu64 for CPU and a coordinated SCARF allocation for GPU; no unbounded download or shared-host load.

Tracking: #66.
